hints.title: Upper Half Implication
hints.text: If the binary representation of x is present in s, then its prefix x >> 1 is also naturally present. Therefore, checking integers in the upper half [n // 2 + 1, n] is sufficient.

hints.title: String Length Feasibility
hints.text: A string of length up to 1000 can contain only a limited number of distinct binary substrings. If n is larger than around 2000, it is impossible for all integers to be present.

hints.title: Direct Substring Verification
hints.text: For numbers from n down to n // 2 + 1, format each as a binary string and verify that it exists as a substring in s. If any binary pattern is absent, return false.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all numbers up to N without pruning large N wastes work when |S| is small.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Checking only numbers in [n/2 + 1, n] cuts checks by half, running quickly within limits.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should observe that binary representation of x contains x // 2 as a prefix.
complexity.notes: Since |S| <= 1000, N > 2048 cannot possibly have all binary patterns in S.
